messages:
sara: quick one — we need a recommendation for how to split our reserved GPU commitment across regions (US-W, EU, APAC) before finance sign-off tomorrow. do we keep heavy in us, or balance?

leo: can you paste the last 30d usage by region and the committed pricing options? i want concrete $/GPU-month numbers.

maria: pulled numbers. short summary: on-demand A100 equivalent: us-west ~ $3.20/hr, eu-west ~ $3.60/hr, apac (singapore) ~ $4.10/hr. committed 1yr reservation discounts: us-west ~ 35%, eu ~ 32%, apac ~ 28%. egress varies — eu->us cross-region egress is expensive for heavy replication.

maria: quick calc (1000 hours/month baseline):
```
region    on-demand/mo   reserved-mo (1yr)   saving/mo per GPU
us-west   $3.20 * 1000 = $3,200   $3,200 * 0.65 = $2,080   = $1,120
eu-west   $3.60 * 1000 = $3,600   $3,600 * 0.68 = $2,448   = $1,152
apac     $4.10 * 1000 = $4,100   $4,100 * 0.72 = $2,952   = $1,148
```
(so absolute savings per GPU similar, but base price higher in apac)

ajay: note availability constraints: H100 pools in eu-west are patchy until next quarter. if we commit in EU we may need to accept A100 taste for some SKUs. also spot preemptions in APAC have been higher — affects job latency SLAs.

leo: thanks. what about effective unit cost after factoring egress and networking for cross-region routing?

maria: good point. if we keep training/ingests in us-west but serve low-latency inference in EU, cross-region KV sync and model repush adds ~ $0.06/token-ish — kidding — but more realistically adds ~ $0.04/token for heavy replication. For our 24/7 serving footprint the monthly egress estimate:
```
assumptions: 200TB/month model sync + 50TB/month traffic egress
us->eu egress rate ~ $0.09/GB -> $200 * 1024 * $0.09 ~ $18k/mo (ballpark)
```
So egress can wipe out reservation savings if we silo wrong.

ajay: TL;DR: commit where the requests originate most and keep cached model shards near consumer. that suggests majority US, a smaller EU pool, and no committed APAC for now — use burst/dedicated on demand there.

leo: finance perspective: propose committed split (by GPU count): US 70%, EU 25%, APAC 5% (burst only). how does that fit with capacity constraints?

maria: fits our 3-week forward demand from product. I ran bin-packing sims with current qps and cold-start rates. US 70% gives us headroom for 99th p99 latency targets. EU 25% covers regional peak + failover. APAC 5% as standby is fine — we should keep an on-demand buffer for H100 on short notice.

infra-bot: Reserved capacity quote generated -> https://billing.example.com/quotes/QR-98233 (1yr, partial upfront).

leo: can you attach the quote PDF to the finance ticket? i'll convert to CAPEX/committed line item. also run a sensitivity scenario if APAC demand grows 2x in six months — how expensive to add commitments later vs now?

maria: yes — quick sensitivity: adding APAC later appears ~15% premium vs negotiating now due to limited supply windows. but our forecast shows low probability of hitting that 2x within 6 months.

ajay: ops note — we'll maintain cross-region cache policy: replicate only hot shards to EU, use async model push for everything else. that should cut egress by ~60%.

leo: ok i'm comfortable with US70/EU25/APAC5 proposal. i'll mark as approved provisional pending legal on contract terms.

sara: awesome — action items: maria to attach detailed sims + sensitivity to ticket, ajay to update routing/cache policy docs, leo to push quote to finance ticket, infra-bot to schedule reserved purchase once legal signs off.

maria: attaching sims in ticket now, linking to perf graphs and p99 traces.

ajay: one more operational flag — set a weekly review for the first 8 weeks post-commit to track utilization and uncommitted spend. put on my calendar.

sara: perfect. thanks team :thumbsup:

leo: noted. moving to finance flow.

infra-bot: purchase scheduled: pending legal -> will auto-execute when flag set.
